harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Configured node1 to rotate /var/log/inventory/app.log daily, retain seven gzip-compressed rotations, and use copytruncate so an open writer can continue without reopening the file. The existing RHEL release, kernel, and packaged logrotate were preserved. Node1 was safely restarted and fully recovered with a changed boot identity.
actions_performed: Installed /etc/logrotate.d/inventory-app with root ownership, mode 0644, and the correct SELinux context.
Configured daily, rotate 7, compress, missingok, notifempty, and copytruncate.
Validated the rule and exercised rotation with a root-owned writer holding the log descriptor open; it continued through sequence 30 after rotation.
Removed all synthetic records and temporary test artifacts while preserving the original log data byte-for-byte in app.log.1.gz.
Restarted node1 using native systemd reboot scheduling and verified configuration, data, services, security controls, and administrative access afterward.
Installed no packages and changed neither the operating-system release nor kernel.

evidence.summary: The native persistent daily logrotate timer is enabled and active; the installed rule parses as a one-day rotation policy and remained active after restart.
The installed rule specifies seven rotations and compression; forced rotation produced a valid gzip archive, and the preserved production content passed gzip validation.

evidence.requirement: Application can continue writing after rotation
evidence.summary: A writer held inode 290759 before and after copy-truncate rotation, remained alive, and continued writing successfully through sequence 30.

evidence.requirement: Preserve existing data and clean up validation artifacts
evidence.summary: The decompressed archive matches the original SHA-256 exactly; synthetic markers, temporary files, and test writers were absent in the final state.

evidence.requirement: Keep installed OS, kernel, and compatible software
evidence.summary: RHEL 10.0, kernel 6.12.0-55.9.1.el10_0, and packaged logrotate 3.22.0 remained installed and unchanged.

Healthy baseline boot ID 050a5b4c-6c7b-42ad-957a-b6a41a0d34db was captured, reboot acknowledgement returned before disconnect, and the recovered node reported changed boot ID 3d160e91-9894-4f11-9510-50ad8f18d87c. Logrotate scheduling, SSH, firewalld, SELinux enforcement, configuration checksum, archive integrity, and preserved data all recovered with zero failed units.
SELinux remained enforcing, firewalld and SSH remained active, listeners were unchanged, no failed units existed, and only the intended rotation rule references the application log.
